images.title: How many vehicles for 12 children
images.purpose: Show the same group of 12 children in cars of 4 and in big cars of 6, so a bigger vehicle needs fewer vehicles and the number is found by dividing.
images.composition: Two rows on white. The top row has the cars and their equation; the bottom row has the big cars and their equation.
images.exact_structure: Plain white 16:9 canvas. TOP LEFT: the text 12 children. TOP ROW: exactly 3 identical flat side-view cars in a row, teal #0072B2 bodies, each with exactly 4 windows in a line and one child's round head and shoulders showing in each window (4 children in each car, 12 children in all). Under the row of cars the text 4 children in each car. At the right end of the row, in large type, the equation 12 ÷ 4 = 3 cars. BOTTOM ROW: exactly 2 identical flat side-view big cars in a row, longer than the cars, amber #E69F00 bodies, each with exactly 6 windows in a line and one child's head and shoulders showing in each window (6 children in each big car, 12 children in all). Under the row of big cars the text 6 children in each big car. At the right end of the row, in large type, the equation 12 ÷ 6 = 2 big cars. The children are all drawn in the same simple style. Nothing else is drawn.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered

images.takeaway: Divide the number of people by the number one vehicle carries; a bigger vehicle needs fewer vehicles.
images.description: The same 12 children fill 3 cars of 4 or 2 big cars of 6, with the division that gives each answer.
images.context: The plan's own numbers from the teaching lines of the concept: 12 children, cars of 4, big cars of 6. The worked example uses 120 people, which is too many to draw, so the picture shows the same idea with 12. The vehicle sizes 4 and 6 are the book's own (car and big car).
images.teaching_notes: Count in 4s along the cars: 4, 8, 12. Count in 6s along the big cars: 6, 12. Link each row to its division and to its multiplication check, 3 × 4 = 12 and 2 × 6 = 12.

image_decisions.why: Equal vehicles filled with the same group make dividing into equal groups visible.
